hunks.baseline: Jeong Hogun led Prince Shangshan and me over to the middle-aged twins, whose names I didn’t know, and sent us a brief Sound Transmission.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun handed Prince Shangshan and me over to the middle-aged twins, whose names I didn’t know, and sent me a brief Sound Transmission.

hunks.baseline: —From now on, you must be careful with every word you say and every move you make. Otherwise, you won’t come out of here alive.
hunks.sol: —From now on, be careful with every word and every move. Otherwise, you won’t leave here alive.

hunks.baseline: I could already feel it in my bones.
Not just because of those twin Supreme Peak masters who’d appeared out of nowhere, but because of all the people inside the palace whose presence I could sense even though we hadn’t entered yet.
hunks.sol: I could already feel the danger on my skin. Not just from the twin Supreme Peak masters who’d appeared out of nowhere, but from all the people inside Qianqing Palace whose presence I could sense before we’d even entered.

hunks.baseline: *This place is insanely well guarded.*
hunks.sol: *This place is guarded like hell.*

hunks.baseline: My mouth felt dry, as if I’d swallowed sand. I slowly drew on my internal energy, carefully enough that no one would notice, and moved my lips.
hunks.sol: My mouth felt as gritty as if I’d swallowed sand. I drew on my internal energy slowly enough that no one would notice, then moved my lips.

hunks.baseline: —Just answer me one thing. Why the hell was I summoned?
hunks.sol: —Just answer me one thing. Why was I summoned?

hunks.baseline: Are you saying you really don’t know, or that you know but won’t tell me?
hunks.sol: —Do you really not know, or do you know but refuse to tell me?

hunks.baseline: I glared at Jeong Hogun, who stood with his usual impassive face, then passed beneath the plaque reading Qianqing Palace alongside Prince Shangshan, who had climbed down from his palanquin.
hunks.sol: I glared at Jeong Hogun, who stood there with his usual impassive face, then passed beneath the plaque reading Qianqing Palace alongside Prince Shangshan, who had climbed down from his palanquin.

hunks.baseline: Clop. Clop.
hunks.sol: Step. Step.

hunks.baseline: I quietly sized up the twins’ backs as they walked in perfect sync, their movements identical down to the smallest detail.
hunks.sol: I studied the twins’ backs as they walked in perfect sync, their movements identical down to the smallest detail.

hunks.baseline: Not being able to guess what martial arts they’d learned was one thing. Just imagining two fully accomplished Supreme Peak masters using a combined attack technique made my stomach hurt.
hunks.sol: Not being able to guess what martial arts they’d learned was one thing. Just imagining two Supreme Peak masters who’d perfected a combined attack technique made my stomach hurt.

hunks.baseline: Shadows that didn’t show even in the faint light.
hunks.sol: Shadows hidden even in the faint light.

hunks.baseline: Those watching our every move from the darkness had to be imperial guards trained by the royal family—and assassins.
hunks.sol: The people watching our every move from the darkness had to be guards raised by the imperial family—and assassins.

hunks.baseline: If the worst came to pass, those assassins, nearly a hundred of them, would carve me up with the one-strike killing techniques they’d spent their lives honing.
hunks.sol: If the worst happened, those assassins, nearly a hundred of them, would carve me up with the one-strike killing techniques they’d spent their lives honing. And the twin Supreme Peak masters would be right there with them, wielding a combined technique they looked as if they’d learned in the womb.

hunks.baseline: Along with the twin Supreme Peak masters, who looked as if they’d learned their combined technique in the womb.

hunks.baseline: *Unless you’re one of the Ten Kings—or maybe a master on par with the Three Saints—you’re almost certainly going to be buried here.*
hunks.sol: *Unless you’re one of the Ten Kings—or maybe a master on par with the Three Saints—you’ll almost certainly be buried here.*

hunks.baseline: The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families might have two Supreme Peak masters at most. Some had only one. And here the Emperor had two of them working as gatekeepers.
hunks.sol: Even the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families had two Supreme Peak masters at most. Usually, they had only one. And here the Emperor had two of them working as gatekeepers.

hunks.baseline: It felt as if I were walking along a blade’s edge.
hunks.sol: I felt as though I were walking along a blade’s edge.

hunks.baseline: Just then, as a bead of cold sweat trickled down the back of my neck before I even realized it, I noticed a small hand tugging at my sleeve.
hunks.sol: A bead of cold sweat slid down the back of my neck. Then I noticed a small hand tugging at my sleeve.

hunks.baseline: A hand gripping so tightly that my sleeve crumpled. Only then did I notice the young prince’s ragged breathing.
hunks.sol: The hand gripped hard enough to crumple the fabric. Only then did I notice the young prince’s ragged breathing.

hunks.baseline: He’d been the same the first time I met him, and nothing had changed now.
hunks.sol: He’d been one when I first met him, and he still was now.

hunks.baseline: He’d said he left the imperial palace when he was so young he couldn’t even remember it. Of course he wouldn’t remember the Son of Heaven, either.
hunks.sol: He’d said he left the imperial palace when he was too young to remember. Of course he wouldn’t remember the Son of Heaven, either.

hunks.baseline: A thought suddenly occurred to me.
hunks.sol: A thought occurred to me.

hunks.baseline: The cheerful side Prince Shangshan had shown on the way to the imperial capital—maybe it was an attempt to hide his fear and disappointment.
hunks.sol: Maybe the cheerful side Prince Shangshan had shown on the way to the Imperial Capital was his way of hiding his fear and disappointment.

hunks.baseline: When Hong Jin warned him that the Son of Heaven was a threat and he shook his head, saying that couldn’t be true…maybe that was the only choice a child could make when faced with a reality too hard to believe.
hunks.sol: When Hong Jin warned him that the Son of Heaven was a threat, he’d shaken his head and said that couldn’t be true. Maybe that was the only response a child could manage when faced with something too painful to believe.

hunks.baseline: *He shouldn’t have to understand any of this…but he’s had to grow up far too soon.*
hunks.sol: *He shouldn’t even have to know about any of this…but he’s had to grow up far too soon.*

hunks.baseline: I thought of the boy from that winter in Shanxi Province, when icy winds howled through the mountains. He’d lost his parents and climbed a hill with his tiny, fern-like hands clinging tight to his little sister.
hunks.sol: I thought of a boy from that winter in Shanxi Province, when icy winds swept through the mountains. He’d lost his parents and climbed a hill, his little fern-like hand gripping his younger sister’s tight.

hunks.baseline: I’d killed the former without a moment’s hesitation. When it came to the latter, I’d even risked my life to help them.
hunks.sol: I’d killed the former without a moment’s hesitation. For the latter, I’d even risked my life.

hunks.baseline: And now, I felt sorry for this young prince.
hunks.sol: And now I felt sorry for this young prince.

hunks.baseline: *I need to think about this coldly. I have to. I can’t afford not to…*
hunks.sol: *I need to think about this coldly. I have to, especially with a choice like this…*

hunks.baseline: Then, almost on impulse, I raised a hand and gently patted his head.
hunks.sol: Then, almost on impulse, I raised a hand and gave his head a couple of gentle pats.

hunks.baseline: His eyes flew wide, and his lips parted slightly, as if he were about to shout that I’d overstepped my bounds. But Prince Shangshan only stared up at me in surprise, his mouth working soundlessly.
hunks.sol: His eyes flew wide, and his lips parted as if he were about to shout that I’d overstepped my bounds. But Prince Shangshan only stared up at me in surprise, his mouth working soundlessly.

hunks.baseline: Instead, the hand that had been gripping my sleeve so tightly loosened, as though he felt relieved.
hunks.sol: Instead, his grip on my sleeve loosened, as though he felt relieved.

hunks.baseline: Even this little thing that every child his age should have experienced was something Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, had probably never known.
hunks.sol: Even something as simple as that—something other children his age took for granted—was probably unfamiliar to Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao.

hunks.baseline: *This is the best I can do for him right now.*
hunks.sol: *And right now, this little bit is the best I can do for him.*

hunks.baseline: Just then, the twins, who had been striding forward without hesitation, stopped in front of a massive door.
hunks.sol: Just then, the twins, who had been striding forward without hesitation, stopped before a massive door.

hunks.baseline: Click. Grrrrr.
hunks.sol: Click. Rumble.

hunks.baseline: With a heavy rumble, an iron door swung open, its surface carved with a dragon so lifelike it seemed to move. The twins, who hadn’t said a word since we entered the palace, broke their silence.
hunks.sol: An iron door swung open with a heavy rumble. A dragon was carved into its surface so vividly it almost seemed alive. The twins, who hadn’t said a word since we entered the palace, broke their silence.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t as though we had any choice left.
Besides, hearing that we’d be separated from the Supreme Peak masters was a welcome surprise.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t as though we had any choice left. Still, hearing that we’d be separated from those Supreme Peak masters was welcome news.

hunks.baseline: The heavy door shut behind us with another rumble. Beneath the faint light of countless night-shining pearls glowing on the ceiling, a man stepped forward.
hunks.sol: The heavy door shut behind us. Beneath the faint light of countless night-shining pearls set into the ceiling, a man stepped forward.

hunks.baseline: Clop.
hunks.sol: Step.

hunks.baseline: A slender frame, as slight as his light footsteps.
hunks.sol: His build was as slight as his footsteps were light.

hunks.baseline: He looked about fifty. A middle-aged man in a long robe whose sleeves dragged along the floor. Prince Shangshan spoke first when he saw him.
hunks.sol: He looked about fifty and wore a long robe with sleeves that dragged along the floor. Prince Shangshan spoke first when he saw him.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man gazed at the tense-faced Prince Shangshan and at me, standing slightly in front of him to shield him. Only when the echoes had faded did he speak.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man gazed at Prince Shangshan’s stiff face, then at me standing slightly in front of him. Only when the echoes faded did he speak.

hunks.baseline: “To see His Highness Prince Shangshan grown so tall, and from so close, fills me with deep emotion after all these years.”
hunks.sol: “To see His Highness Prince Shangshan so grown, and from this close, moves me deeply after all these years.”

hunks.baseline: After hesitating, Prince Shangshan asked, “Do you…know me?”
hunks.sol: After a moment’s hesitation, Prince Shangshan asked, “Do you…know me?”

hunks.baseline: A faint smile appeared on his wrinkled lips. The man turned his gaze from Prince Shangshan to me.
hunks.sol: A faint smile touched his wrinkled lips. He turned his gaze from Prince Shangshan to me.

hunks.baseline: “You’re a stranger to me.”
hunks.sol: “You and I have never met.”

hunks.baseline: I chose silence instead of answering. The moment I saw him, I’d had to fight to keep a string of curses from spilling out.
hunks.sol: I said nothing. The moment I saw him, I’d had to fight to keep a string of curses from spilling out.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man in front of me—no, this middle-aged man, too—was a Supreme Peak master.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man in front of me—no, this middle-aged man *too*—was a Supreme Peak master.

hunks.baseline: *No, fuck me… This is so goddamn unfair.*
hunks.sol: *Oh, for fuck’s sake… I can’t do this anymore.*

hunks.baseline: I’d only been at the imperial palace for two days.
hunks.sol: This was only my second day at the imperial palace.

hunks.baseline: And that was being generous. If you counted the actual time I’d spent here, it hadn’t even been twelve shichen—a full day.
hunks.sol: And even that was being generous. I hadn’t actually been here for twelve shichen, a full day.

hunks.baseline: And yet this was already the fifth Supreme Peak master I’d come face-to-face with.
hunks.sol: Yet this was already the fifth Supreme Peak master I’d come face-to-face with.

hunks.baseline: Just as I was seriously wondering if I should start wearing a condom instead of clothes, the middle-aged man spoke again.
hunks.sol: I was seriously wondering if I should start wearing a condom instead of clothes when the man spoke again.

hunks.baseline: “The imperial court’s eyes and ears are everywhere. And you do stand out.”
hunks.sol: “The imperial family’s eyes and ears are everywhere. And you do stand out.”

hunks.baseline: Listen to the way this guy talks.
hunks.sol: Listen to this guy.

hunks.baseline: “Then what do you do around here? The eyes? Or the ears?”
hunks.sol: “Then what are you around here? The eyes? Or the ears?”

hunks.baseline: “Your sleeves are dragging on the floor, so I figure you must be great at mopping.”
hunks.sol: “Your sleeves are dragging along the floor. I bet you could give it a hell of a polish.”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man stared at me blankly for a moment, then burst out laughing.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man stared at me blankly for a moment, then laughed aloud.

hunks.baseline: “Of course, the stories I heard were all over the place, so I was curious myself. Now, this way.”
hunks.sol: “Of course, the accounts were all over the place, so I was curious myself. Now, this way.”

hunks.baseline: Without giving me a chance to answer, the middle-aged man spun around and naturally took the lead, not even looking back.
hunks.sol: Before I could answer, he turned and took the lead as if it were only natural, without so much as a glance back.

hunks.baseline: *Obviously, he wasn’t a cleaner.*
hunks.sol: *Obviously, he isn’t a cleaner.*

hunks.baseline: Who the hell was he? His clothes didn’t offer much of a clue.
hunks.sol: Who the hell was he? His clothes offered no clue.

hunks.baseline: The East Depot? Or the Embroidered Uniform Guard?
hunks.sol: East Depot? Or Embroidered Uniform Guard?

hunks.baseline: His gaunt frame made him look more like a eunuch, but his voice was so weighty it could knock even an Embroidered Uniform Guard off his feet.
hunks.sol: His gaunt frame made him look more like a eunuch, but his voice was weighty enough to put an Embroidered Uniform Guard to shame.

hunks.baseline: And there was the way he moved around as naturally as if this were his own home.
hunks.sol: And he moved around as naturally as if this were his own home.

hunks.baseline: *Even the twins didn’t come this far. So he must be one of the Emperor’s closest, most trusted confidants…*
hunks.sol: *Even the twins didn’t come this far. So he must be one of the Emperor’s closest, most trusted people…*

hunks.baseline: The guards, of course, as well as the eunuchs and palace attendants who stayed inside to see to every need…
hunks.sol: There were the guards, of course, along with the eunuchs and palace attendants who stayed inside to see to his every need.

hunks.baseline: This place had been created for the Emperor, by the Emperor, and in service of the Emperor.
hunks.sol: This place existed for the Emperor, by the Emperor, and in service of the Emperor.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know for sure, but he’d probably need to be close in standing to Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t be sure, but he’d probably have to hold a position close to Baek Yeon’s as Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

hunks.baseline: *Then could this guy be the East Depot’s leader, the Director? No. I heard he was much older, and that he’d been bedridden with illness for years.*
hunks.sol: *Could this be the Director, the head of the East Depot? No. I heard he was much older, and he’s been bedridden with illness for years.*

hunks.baseline: I quickly racked my brain, but no one came to mind.
hunks.sol: I racked my brain, but no one came to mind.

hunks.baseline: Ma Sanbao had mentioned far too many people, and the man didn’t match the distinctive features of any of the few he’d described.
hunks.sol: Ma Sanbao had mentioned far too many people, and this man didn’t match the distinctive features of any of the few he’d described.

hunks.baseline: But there was nothing I could do about that.
hunks.sol: But there was nothing I could do about that. If I wanted answers, I’d have to get them myself.

hunks.baseline: If you’re thirsty, you dig a well.
I’d just have to pry the information out of him somehow.
Walking behind the middle-aged man as he strolled along at an unhurried pace, I tossed out a question.
hunks.sol: I followed the man as he strolled along at an unhurried pace and tossed out a question.

hunks.baseline: “When do I get to meet the Emperor?”
hunks.sol: “When do I get to meet His Majesty?”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man gave a quiet laugh without looking back.
hunks.sol: The man gave a short laugh without looking back.

hunks.baseline: “You’re as impatient as you look. Just wait a little. His Majesty is enjoying a rare diversion.”
hunks.sol: “You’re as impatient as you look. Wait a little. His Majesty is enjoying a diversion he hasn’t had in some time.”

hunks.baseline: “Enjoying a diversion? After summoning us?”
hunks.sol: “A diversion? After summoning us?”

hunks.baseline: “Everyone has a place of their own. To ascend the throne means to look down upon them all. Isn’t that a simple and straightforward truth of the world?”
hunks.sol: “Everyone has their place. To ascend the throne is to be able to look down upon them all. A simple enough truth of the world, isn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: Not because I objected to the Emperor’s behavior, or because the middle-aged man’s answer had struck a nerve.
hunks.sol: Not because I objected to the Emperor’s behavior, or because the man’s answer had struck a nerve.

hunks.baseline: It was the casual look and tone he’d just shown me. The effortless confidence that came through in every small movement.
And on top of that, he didn’t look anything like any of the Emperor’s confidants Ma Sanbao had mentioned.
hunks.sol: It was the casual look on his face, his tone, the effortless authority in every small movement. And on top of that, his appearance didn’t match any of the Emperor’s confidants Ma Sanbao had mentioned.

hunks.baseline: The moment I let out a quiet groan inwardly—
hunks.sol: The thought sent a groan through me.

hunks.baseline: Clop.
hunks.sol: Step.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man came to an abrupt stop. He threw open the door before them, decorated with gold, silver, and jewels, without the slightest hesitation, then spoke.
hunks.sol: The man came to an abrupt stop. Without a moment’s hesitation, he threw open the door before him, decorated with gold, silver, and jewels.

hunks.baseline: But there was no answer from anywhere.
hunks.sol: But there was no answer.

hunks.baseline: In fact, there wasn’t a hint of anyone else’s presence.
hunks.sol: In fact, I couldn’t sense anyone else at all.

hunks.baseline: Only one person stood within this enormous bedchamber.
hunks.sol: Only one person stood inside the enormous bedchamber.

hunks.baseline: He slowly turned around. Then he smiled at us, showing his white teeth.
hunks.sol: He turned slowly toward us and smiled, showing his white teeth.
